characters.name: Amaia
characters.description: Taíno woman leading a night river escape by canoe; mother of a son not yet two; has stopped saying the names of the lost. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Amaia had started the night with fourteen.

characters.name: Dairon
characters.description: Amaia's brother; leads the first canoe through the mangroves; described as having spent all his fear. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Her brother Dairon took the lead canoe through the mangroves

characters.name: Yara
characters.description: Rides behind Dairon carrying the wrapped cemí against her chest. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Yara rode behind him with the wrapped cemí against her chest

characters.name: Beheto
characters.description: Drummer in the second canoe; lungs rattle when he breathes hard; his timing 'had never once been wrong'; plays the asking rhythm to the river. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: Beheto, whose lungs rattled when he breathed hard and whose timing had never once been wrong

characters.name: The behique
characters.description: Mentioned-only shamanic figure who calls the three glowing children 'the lit ones'. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: The behique called them the lit ones.

characters.name: The lit ones (three children)
characters.description: Collective ensemble of three children in the third canoe who emit a thin blue light when they flinch; includes a seven-year-old girl who speaks to the water and a nine-year-old who hears the bell. Third child's identity unspecified.
characters.evidence: In the third, three children sat so still it was worse than crying.

characters.name: Amaia's son
characters.description: Amaia's son, not yet two, who sleeps against her ribs and speaks in a voice too old for him. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: Her own son, not yet two, slept against her ribs.

characters.name: The man with the brass bell
characters.description: One of the pursuers on the bank; carries a small brass bell on a pole and rings it; the sound is flat and wrong. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: One carried a small brass bell on a pole and rang it

characters.name: The man with the book
characters.description: Pursuer sitting on a stump writing in a book as the canoes slide away; counts the escapees 'the way you count sacks'. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: Another man sat on a stump with a book across his knee and wrote in it as the canoes slid away

characters.name: The trailing men
characters.description: Collective ensemble of men who trailed the fleeing families for two months and stop on the bank. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: the men who had trailed them for two months had stopped.

characters.name: Juan Carlos
characters.description: First-person narrator; a broke software/mural artist living on the fourth floor over Jerome Avenue; builds the Chismosa module; breaks it at 3:07 a.m. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: “Juan Carlos.” Through the wood, not a question.

characters.name: Mamá (narrator's mother)
characters.description: Lives two rooms over; prays the rosary in her sleep; knocks twice and decides not to ask questions. Physical appearance unspecified.

characters.name: The narrator's grandmother
characters.description: Mentioned-only; gave the narrator the coin at twelve; calls its markings señales viejas. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: my grandmother calls señales viejas, old signs

characters.name: Manny
characters.description: The narrator's friend; texts at 2:41 while riding the 6 home from a quince in Mott Haven; knows the narrator too accurately. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Manny texted at 2:41, riding the 6 home from a quince in Mott Haven.

characters.name: The Ballroom dancers
characters.description: Collective ensemble of roughly forty couples of light, men in two-tone shoes, women with skirts catching air, dancing in the 1957 Ballroom; they go still when the eight-second loop hits. Individual dancers unnamed.
characters.evidence: Couples. Forty, maybe, built out of nothing but light and the shape of light

characters.name: The Ballroom band
characters.description: Collective ensemble heard in the vision: horn section, unhurried cowbell player, shoes on wood; keeps playing as the dancers freeze. Members unnamed.
characters.evidence: a horn section, a cowbell somebody was riding without any hurry

characters.name: The man in the lit window
characters.description: Unmoving figure with headphones standing in the third-floor window of the empty building across the street, facing the narrator's building during the blackout. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: A man stood in it, not moving, headphones on, facing our building

characters.name: Mentioned Bronx neighbors and locals
characters.description: Mentioned-only collective: the lady on three (Pyrex owner), two guys not speaking since a bodega fight, the super and his biting dog, a bitten delivery guy, a kid on the stoop, a kid awaiting his EP, a laughing woman in the Ballroom. Physical appearances unspecified.
characters.evidence: Two guys I’d known since I was nine, not speaking.

scenes.name: BEFORE: The river escape at night
scenes.description: Historical BEFORE section, 1957-era Taíno flight: three canoes slip through mangroves by night; pursuers ring a brass bell and write in a book from the bank; the lit children flinch blue; Beheto's drum asks the river; the current turns and the river gives them to the sea.
scenes.evidence: Before any of this there was a river, and a woman who was done counting.

scenes.name: 3:07: The confession and the room
scenes.description: The narrator admits breaking the software on purpose at 3:07 a.m., then sets the room: fourth floor over Jerome Avenue, the 4 train, the cracked window, the coin on the nightstand and its señales viejas.
scenes.evidence: At 3:07 on a Tuesday morning in March, I took a perfectly good piece of software and broke it on purpose.

scenes.name: Chismosa, the spiral, and the eight-second loop
scenes.description: The narrator explains the Ballroom mural gig, the Chismosa module listening to the steam riser, the recurring spiral-and-triangle shape, the ugly eight-second loop, and the block's little-mean month.
scenes.evidence: I called it Chismosa, because all it did was listen to the building and tell me the gossip.

scenes.name: Manny's text and deleting the filter stack
scenes.description: Manny texts at 2:41; after three cafecitos the narrator deletes Chismosa's entire filter stack and points the raw feed at the projector; ears pop, the air gets heavy, and the static pulls into a point.
scenes.evidence: I opened the config and deleted all of it.

scenes.name: The Ballroom, 1957: ECHO vision
scenes.description: ECHO section: the wall opens into the 1957 Ballroom; forty light-built couples dance around the inlaid spiral and triangle; the eight-second loop comes up the pipe and flattens the dancers one pair at a time while the band keeps playing; the coin lifts off the nightstand, hot.
scenes.evidence: They were dancing in the Ballroom, in my building, a floor under my feet and almost seventy years down

scenes.name: Blackout, Mamá's knock, and the lit window
scenes.description: The apartment cuts out; the dancers stay lit two seconds more, then go; Mamá knocks and decides not to ask; the whole block is dark except one third-floor window in the empty building across the street, where a man with headphones stands facing them.
